correctness.rationale: For every integer b,k>=2 and time t>=0, the unique-flow identity for a tree and the exact intertwining e^{-tBB^T}B=Be^{-tB^TB} reduce the optimal W1 coefficient to edge-column sums. The explicitly multiplied incidence matrix has a leaf-contrast eigenvalue one and two 2-by-2 edge blocks on constant and branch-standard modes. Counting the entries in each of the two edge orbits yields the stated I and O formulas with all absolute values. For b=k=N, Metzler comparison reduces I to two scalar mode sums, the standard slow mode has coefficient 2-3/N+O(N^-2), and the time 3 log N/N matches the uniform inner-row upper bound. A uniform O<=3+2/sqrt(N) bound prevents the other orbit from controlling the large-N peak. Continuous-time heat-kernel positivity proves strict nonattainment of diameter four at finite N. The actual CHECKER.py file replayed all reported full-matrix comparisons, tree-flow computations and transport LPs; finite tests do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: Depth-two regular trees are a natural test family for heat-semigroup Wasserstein contraction beyond the star. The theorem exactly compresses an operator whose edge dimension grows quadratically to two fixed-size exponentials for all parameters and times. The sharp 4-10/N maximal-amplification law shows a precise approach to the geometric diameter barrier at a vanishing time scale while proving finite nonattainment, a structural phenomenon not supplied by abstract curvature bounds. The all-time formula is useful even when the two edge-orbit contributions exchange dominance. The result does not claim weighted, degree-normalized, or higher-depth trees.
